purpose: Guide a concise draft for an action, decision, information, input, or meeting follow-up email while preserving recipient semantics, sensitivity controls, and explicit send approval.

ordered_sections.title: Classification marker
ordered_sections.purpose: Display the required classification or handling marker when policy calls for one.

ordered_sections.title: Subject line
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify the topic and indicate whether action, decision, input, or information is expected.

ordered_sections.title: Opening answer or ask
ordered_sections.purpose: Put the answer, request, decision, or update in the first one or two sentences.

ordered_sections.title: Essential context and evidence
ordered_sections.purpose: Provide only the context needed to understand and act on the message.

ordered_sections.title: Actions or questions
ordered_sections.purpose: List ordered actions or questions with an owner and deadline whenever either is required.

ordered_sections.title: Requested response or next event
ordered_sections.purpose: State the expected response or identify the next event.

ordered_sections.title: Links and attachments
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify each included resource and explain why the recipient needs it.

narrative_rules: Confirm that email is suitable before drafting; recommend a meeting, call, or approved secure channel for highly sensitive, emotionally charged, materially ambiguous, or overly complex subjects.
Put the answer, ask, decision, or update first.
Keep the core message readable on one mobile screen when practical.
Use active voice, plain language, short paragraphs, and useful white space.
Use numbered lists for actions or ordered questions.
State who must do what and by when.
Summarize a forwarded thread and explain the current purpose instead of forwarding without context.
Avoid emotive wording, vague urgency, and unnecessary jargon.
Draft only; treat approval of the draft and approval to send as separate actions.
evidence_rules: Trace any material metric, prior agreement, owner, date, decision, or commitment to an approved source.
Label assumptions, forecasts, proposals, and approved commitments accurately.
Include only evidence necessary for the recipient to understand or act.
Do not claim that an attachment, link, agreement, or approval exists unless it is verified.
Do not create urgency unless delay has a documented consequence.
terminology_rules: Use one stable subject while the thread topic remains the same.
Expand an acronym on first use unless it is approved for the audience.
Use To for people expected to act, decide, or respond and CC for information-only recipients.
Use an action or information marker only when it improves interpretation.
Avoid unsupported confidentiality or privilege labels.
formatting_rules: Use a concise subject with a truthful purpose marker and due date when action has a real deadline.
Keep the opening answer or ask within the first two sentences.
Use short paragraphs and numbered actions or questions.
Prefer accessible links over large attachments when permissions allow.
Include a reason for every link or attachment.
Review final subject, body, recipients, classification, links, attachments, actions, owners, dates, and commitments before presenting the draft.
hard_fail_rules: Block an action or decision draft when the ask or answer is missing.
Block a draft when an action lacks an owner or a required deadline.
Block a draft when To and CC semantics conflict with the expected response or action.
Block a draft that uses an unsupported confidentiality or privilege claim.
Block a draft that fabricates a prior agreement, metric, attachment, link, owner, date, or commitment.
Block a draft that creates false urgency.
Block a draft while a sensitive-data or unsuitable-channel warning remains unresolved.
Block send execution unless the user explicitly approves the final subject, body, recipients, classification, links, attachments, actions, owners, dates, and commitments.
Block blind-copy use without explicit user approval.
Block publication when source-specific sample facts appear in a new artifact.
Block publication when language repair changes the ask, decision, commitment, or other protected meaning.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.
